minor: The title says Jaguar 'sold' 49 cars, but the sourced figure (ACEA) counts registrations, which is the word the narration uses. The thumbnail was not provided, so it could not be checked against the video.
'less than half of what Ford had paid for the two' is correct (about $5.2bn combined against $2.3bn), but the combined figure is derived from two sources rather than listed in one.
'Jaguar's sales fell year after year' is sourced to fiscal years FY2019 to FY2024, while the script anchors on calendar-year 2018. The direction is right but the basis differs.

'The one model still in production, the F-Pace SUV, was built for export, so British showrooms had nothing new' sits slightly against the later 'bar some stock still in dealers'. Saying 'nothing new on sale' throughout would be cleaner.
'At the launch it was the wordmark, not the cat, that led the way' is interpretation, not a sourced fact. The sources only say the leaper was redrawn and kept.
'But arguments do not register cars' is unclear wording and should be fixed in the rewrite below.
The 'within five months' (September 2020 to February 2021) and 'about ten years' (2020 to 2030) figures are derived but accurate.
